title: Drizzle in five minutes
description: Create, read, update and delete posts, compare query shapes, then keep related writes together.

steps.label: Tables
steps.title: Meet your tables
steps.body:
You manage a small blog with Drizzle ORM **1.0.0-rc.5** on PostgreSQL. Drizzle Run provides the connection so you can focus on the API.

`schema.ts` declares `users` and `posts` with `pgTable`. A **primary key** identifies each row. The post's `authorId` references `users.id`, so each post must point to an existing user.

Every **Run** starts fresh: create tables, run `seed.ts`, then run `query.ts`. Press **Run** to meet Ada, Grace and Linus.

meta.summary: Three users and three posts, written by `seed.ts` before every run.

steps.label: Insert
steps.title: Publish Ada's next post
steps.body:
Use `.insert(posts).values()` to publish a post. You supply its title and Ada's user ID, `1`. The `serial` column generates the post ID.

`.returning()` gives you an array of inserted rows, including generated values. Press **Run**: **Published post** contains one row with ID `4`.

meta.summary: Supply a title and author; return the generated post ID.
meta.changed: You supplied the title and author. PostgreSQL generated ID `4` for Learning Drizzle.

steps.label: Select
steps.title: Find Ada's posts
steps.body:
Select just `id` and `title`. `.where(eq(posts.authorId, 1))` keeps Ada's posts; `.orderBy(desc(posts.id))` puts higher IDs first.

This step replaces the insert with a select. Each run starts from the seed, so the post you inserted in step 2 is gone. Press **Run**: you get Notes, then Hello. Open **SQL** to inspect the selected columns, filter and ordering.

meta.summary: Pick two columns, filter by author, and order by ID.
meta.changed: Only Ada's seeded posts remain: Notes (`2`), then Hello (`1`).

steps.label: Relations
steps.title: Load users with their posts
steps.body:
On the **SQL-like** side, `leftJoin` matches `posts.authorId` to `users.id`. Choose this shape when you want flat rows: Ada appears once per post.

The **relational query builder (RQB)** returns each user with a nested posts array. `defineRelations` describes those connections for `db.query`; it does not replace the database's foreign key.

Press **Run**. Linus has no posts: the left join keeps him with a `null` title, and RQB returns an empty posts array.

meta.summary: Compare flat joined rows with nested relational results.
meta.changed: Both sides keep Linus: a null title in the join, an empty posts array in RQB.

steps.label: Update
steps.title: Update and delete
steps.body:
Back to one editor. `.update().set()` renames post `1`; `.delete()` removes post `3`. Each `.where()` selects a post by ID. `.returning()` gives back the changed rows.

**Without .where(), an update or delete affects every row in the table.** In your own project, [Drizzle's ESLint plugin](https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/eslint-plugin) can flag missing filters. It cannot tell whether your filter selects the intended rows.

Press **Run**: Hello becomes Hello, Drizzle; Ships is deleted; Notes stays.

meta.summary: Rename a post and delete another, with `.returning()`.

steps.label: Transaction
steps.title: Keep both changes or neither
steps.body:
A **transaction** keeps a group of writes together: they all commit, or they are undone. Use `tx` for both writes inside `db.transaction`.

The first transaction renames Hello and deletes Ships, then calls `tx.rollback()`. That throws a rollback error, which we catch outside the transaction. Both changes are undone.

The second transaction repeats the same writes without rolling back. Press **Run**: **After rollback** has the original three posts; **After commit** has Hello, Drizzle and Notes.

meta.summary: Compare the same writes rolled back and committed.
meta.changed: Rollback kept all three original posts. Commit kept the rename and deletion together.

steps.label: Your turn
steps.title: Find Grace's posts yourself
steps.body:
The editor is back to the filtered select, and the next run starts from the original seed. Choose **Finish guide** to unlock the editor.

Change the author ID in `.where()` from `1` to `2`, change the display label to Grace's posts, then press **Run**. You should get one row: Ships, with ID `3`.

Use **Fork to my projects** if you want to keep your changes. Next, explore [relational queries](https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/rqb) in more depth.

meta.summary: Finish the guide, filter by author ID `2`, and run. Expect Ships (`3`).
meta.changed: Your turn: filter by author ID `2` and run. Expect Ships (`3`). Fork to keep your changes.
